subject: Re: Feature parity + next tests (tool-calling, structured output, streaming)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Jenkins <ben.jenkins@acme.com>, Laura Kim <laura.kim@acme.com>
Cc: Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Quick recap + next steps (tool-calling, structured outputs, streaming)

Thanks Ben & Laura — great conversation earlier. Wanted to capture the key takeaways and proposed next steps so we’re all aligned:

Summary from call:
- Use case: Acme search assistant that calls internal tools (product catalog API) and returns structured JSON for downstream ingestion.
- Top priorities: reliable function/tool calling, deterministic structured outputs (schema adherence), and sub-300ms streaming-first-token latency for short queries.
- Current competitive evaluation: you’ve run tests against hyperscaler endpoints (VendorX, MegaCloud) and one self-hosted runtime. You want to compare output correctness, schema validation rates, and latency/streaming behavior.

Proposed next tests (we can own the execution):
1) Tool/function-calling: run 50 representative sessions from your audit logs (we’ll use the provided inputs) and check invocation routing, arguments extraction, and end-to-end success.
2) Structured outputs: validate against your JSON schema; measure % of responses that pass strict schema and a relaxed schema.
3) Streaming: measure time-to-first-token and completion latency for short (<=30 token) queries across 200 requests.

Acceptance criteria (draft):
- Tool-calling: >=95% correct argument extraction and no silent failures (errors surfaced).
- Schema pass rate: >=90% strict, >=98% relaxed.
- Streaming TTF token: median <300ms for US region.

Attachments: I’m including a feature parity matrix template and a test input bundle stub (redwood_feature-parity-matrix.xlsx, acme_tool-calling-test-inputs.json). We’ll update with results and raw logs.

Next steps:
- Ben: confirm the sample of 50 tool-calling sessions and share any restricted fields to scrub.
- Laura: share the production JSON schema you want validated.
- We’ll schedule a 60-min test kickoff with Monica (SE) and David (solutions) — proposed windows below.

Proposed kickoff slots (PST): Wed 07/07 10:00–11:00, Thu 07/08 13:00–14:00, Tue 07/13 09:00–10:00. Tell us what works and we’ll send calendar invites.

Thanks — excited to run these and show the practical differences.

—
Marissa Cole

Thanks Marissa — this is super helpful. Quick clarifications: 

- We can share the 50 tool sessions, but two of them contain PII that needs to be redacted. I’ll send the scrubbed bundle by EOD Monday (07/05).
- On the schema: Laura will confirm which version (v2.1) to use — we’ll attach that in the next message.
- About hyperscaler differences: could you briefly call out the specific behavioral differences we should expect vs. VendorX/MegaCloud? In particular we care about: (a) function-call deterministic arg extraction (they had 80–85% on our tests), (b) how you expose streaming vs. chunked polling, and (c) any concurrency limits that could impact our throughput.

Also — procurement question: our legal team asked if Redwood supports SOC 2 Type II and whether we can provide the latest report during the evaluation.

Appreciate it. Will send scrubbed inputs and the schema.

Ben

ben.jenkins@acme.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Jenkins <ben.jenkins@acme.com>, Laura Kim <laura.kim@acme.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>, Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 01 Jul 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick recap + next steps (tool-calling, structured outputs, streaming)

Thanks Ben — answers inline and looping in Monica & David to own test execution: 

- Deterministic function-calling: Redwood’s runtime favors explicit tool-call schema enforcement. In our internal tests we typically see >95% correct arg extraction on well-formed prompts and >=90% on messy/noisy inputs. We’ll instrument a strict parser and report arg-extraction accuracy per test.
- Streaming vs chunked polling: Redwood supports true server-sent streaming over HTTP/2/HTTP3 with token-level push (we’ll measure time-to-first-token). By contrast, some hyperscalers provide chunked HTTP responses or require client polling — that’s likely why you saw slower TTF in VendorX. We’ll include a streaming demo for your frontend (React example).
- Concurrency: for the Dedicated plan we can reserve GPU pools with predictable concurrency; for the hosted API we currently support per-tenant concurrency controls and can surface per-route limits. For the short evaluation, concurrency won’t be constrained — we’ll emulate your target QPS. Monica will share exact config.
- SOC 2: yes, we can provide our latest SOC 2 Type II report under NDA. I’ll send next steps to procurement separately (cc: Avery).

Monica — can you draft the test plan and include the exact API calls we’ll run (tool-call + streaming harness + schema validator)? David — please capture the expected infra profile and whether we should run tests from Hosted vs Dedicated nodes.

I’ll hold on calendar invites until we confirm slots.

—
Marissa
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Jenkins <ben.jenkins@acme.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>

Subject: Test plan: tool-calling + schema validation + streaming (draft)

Hi all — attaching the draft test plan and the input bundle (attached as acme_tool-calling-test-inputs.json). High level: 

1) Tool-calling test
- Run 50 sessions: we’ll replay prompts through Redwood’s API with your tool spec.
- Metrics: arg-extraction accuracy, false-invocation rate, error surface count, end-to-end success (tool returned expected output).
- Output artifacts: per-session logs, extracted args JSON, invocation traces.

2) Schema validation
- Run responses through your strict v2.1 schema validator and our relaxed validator (whitelist of nullable fields).
- Metrics: strict pass rate, relaxed pass rate, top 10 failing fields with examples.

3) Streaming performance
- 200 short queries (<=30 tokens) from three client regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west).
- Metrics: time-to-first-token, median completion latency, token throughput.

Execution notes:
- We will run tests in Hosted first (to mirror your earlier VendorX runs) then repeat on a Dedicated node if you want to see reserved-capacity behavior.
- We will publish a short results digest and a full artifact bundle in the shared Drive link.

Attachments: acme_tool-calling-test-inputs.json, redwood_feature-parity-matrix.xlsx (template).

Please confirm the scrubbed inputs and the schema link. Once Ben confirms we’ll schedule the first run (should take ~3 hours to execute + 24–48 hours for analysis).

Thanks — Monica
